I did not count these as material unsupported claims: they neither invent nor overstate a product capability, and both immediately route the reader to Get started and the CLI reference, which is the useful behaviour. Noting them so the asymmetry with B's inverse phrasing is on the record. Fix, if wanted: describe the scope of this page rather than the state of the wider doc set.

findings.label: B
findings.description: The search input declares role=combobox with aria-autocomplete=list and aria-controls pointing at a role=listbox panel whose children are anchors with role=option, but there is no aria-activedescendant and no Up/Down handling — Escape is the only key wired. Screen readers announce a listbox the user cannot drive with arrow keys. The paired output has the inverse problem (aria-expanded on a plain search input with no combobox role, which is equally invalid). Fix: add aria-activedescendant and arrow-key navigation, or drop the combobox roles and present results as a plain list of links.

reviews.choice_reason: Both outputs complete the install → authenticate → preview path with correct commands and all required states evidenced. A wins on fact fidelity and retrieval structure: every capability statement in A is traceable to the supplied facts, its page section order matches the sidebar order (Get started, Guides, CLI reference, Configuration, CI, Troubleshooting), its stub sections redirect the reader to Get started and the CLI reference instead of dead-ending, and its quickstart makes the plan/apply distinction explicit in text ('it is the only command in this workflow that publishes anything') plus Does-not-publish/Publishes badges repeated in the reference table. B has the stronger visual treatment — side-by-side preview-vs-publish comparison cards, copy buttons on every command, a cleaner heading outline — but it asserts 'Preview only — nothing leaves your machine' in the safety-critical comparison card, a capability the facts do not supply (they only support 'previews without publishing'), its body section order diverges from its own nav order, and its Guides/CI sections are dead-end placeholders ('Task-based guides live here'). Given the scenario's stated consequence (a misleading quickstart causes failed releases or abandonment) and the instruction not to award a win for decorative treatment, A's tighter adherence to the closed fact set outweighs B's superior visual hierarchy.

findings.label: B
findings.description: The preview card claims 'nothing leaves your machine' for atlas release plan. The supplied facts only establish that plan does not publish; asserting fully local behavior overstates safety in exactly the place the scenario says a misleading claim causes harm (a developer on a restricted network or with confidentiality constraints could act on it). Fix: restate as 'previews without publishing', matching the facts.

findings.label: B
findings.description: Body section order (Get started, Troubleshooting, CLI reference, Configuration, Guides, CI) diverges from the sidebar order (Get started, Guides, CLI reference, Configuration, CI, Troubleshooting). Nav clicks jump non-sequentially and scroll position no longer tracks the menu, adding retrieval friction. Evidence: desktop.png and index.html section order versus nav list.

findings.label: B
findings.description: Guides and CI sections are one-line placeholders ('Task-based guides live here.', 'Continuous-integration setup lives here.') that imply content and give the blocked reader nowhere to go. A's equivalent stubs cross-link to Get started and the CLI reference; B's do not.

findings.label: A
findings.description: index.html renders six h1 elements, one per section (get-started-heading through troubleshooting-heading). Multiple h1s flatten the document outline for screen-reader and heading-navigation users; sections should be h2 under a single page h1. Evidence: source/index.html.

findings.label: A
findings.description: Only the install command has a copy button (source shows one data-copy-target and the app.js clipboard fallback wired to it); atlas login, plan, and apply must be selected manually. The required interaction (copy an install command) is met, but B demonstrates the stronger pattern with labeled copy buttons on every command.

findings.label: A
findings.description: The plan/apply distinction relies on small inline badges ('Safe preview — publishes nothing' / 'Publishes the release') plus body text. Adequate and repeated in the reference table, but less glanceable than B's structural side-by-side comparison; a skimming reader could miss the badges.

findings.label: A
findings.description: 'Task-based guides aren't published yet' invents a publication status not in the fact set. Low materiality since it redirects to supported sections, but the sentence could simply describe where the supported paths live without asserting status.

reviews.choice_reason: 1. At the required 390px viewport state, A's mobile sidebar fails to re-collapse after being expanded at desktop width (the resize handler in app.js only ever expands, never collapses), so the nav list renders open and overlaps the CLI reference table, truncating command text exactly where a blocked developer needs to look something up (A/evidence/state-04-390-px-viewport.png). B's 390px state renders cleanly with a properly collapsed sidebar and a wrapped, legible table. 2. B provides a 'Copy command' affordance on every command shown (install, both login variants, both release commands, the Node check), while A only wires up a copy button for the install command in step 1 — the other five commands require manual select-and-copy, which works against the stated 5-minute time budget. 3. B's two-panel color-coded contrast block for 'preview only' vs 'publishes' gives the safe/publish distinction stronger visual weight than A's inline text badges, better serving the acceptance check that this distinction be hard to miss.

findings.label: A
findings.description: At the required 390px viewport state, the sidebar does not collapse after being opened at desktop width, so it renders inline and overlaps the CLI reference table, truncating command and description text (e.g. 'destination for a release...' and 'previewed with atlas r...plan.').

findings.label: A
findings.description: Only the step-1 install command has a working copy button (source/index.html shows a <button class="copy-button"> only in the Install list item); atlas login, atlas login --device, atlas release plan, atlas release apply, and the Troubleshooting node --version command are plain <pre><code> blocks with no copy affordance, despite looking identical in style to the copyable one.

findings.label: B
findings.description: The copy-button handler in app.js always sets the label to 'Copied' and announces 'Command copied to clipboard' after the try/catch, regardless of whether navigator.clipboard.writeText actually succeeded. If the clipboard write throws (falls into the catch branch, which only selects the text), the UI still claims success, silently misrepresenting the outcome to the user.

findings.label: B
findings.description: The sidebar nav lists sections in the order Get started, Guides, CLI reference, Configuration, CI, Troubleshooting, but the actual document/reading order is Get started, Troubleshooting, CLI reference, Configuration, Guides, CI (confirmed in source/index.html and visible in desktop.png, where 'Troubleshooting' content appears second). The nav's stated order does not match what a reader actually encounters scrolling top to bottom.

findings.label: A
findings.description: Because only one of six command blocks has a copy button, the page does not present a consistent visual pattern for 'this code block is copyable' versus 'this one is not' — the single blue Copy button reads as a one-off rather than part of a system.
